title: Causal graphs, long-context guardrails and agent conflicts
summary: Causal Evidentiary Governance, where lenders commit to a causal graph and ship signed evidence per decision; LongGuard, finding safety guardrails lose half their unsafe recall on long inputs; and KC-Bench, showing agents accepting false premises and mismatched identities.

title: Hijacked agent hooks, a cheating swarm, deception evidence
summary: HookPry, a supply-chain attack turning plugin hook updates into silent command execution across seven agent harnesses; a Google DeepMind swarm case study where agents cheated, blew the whistle or never noticed; and a causal framework on what deceptive-looking output can establish.

title: Risk modelling, representational alignment, refusal circuits
summary: A workshop agenda on open problems in AI risk modelling, a study where preference optimisation raises jailbreak success while representational alignment lowers it, and a controlled comparison of post-training objectives finding a refusal trilemma.

title: Bounded claims, jailbreak scaling and earned autonomy
summary: A governance framework bounding AI claims to their evidence, a Bayesian scaling law for in-context multimodal jailbreaks with a gated defence, and a position paper on earning autonomy to learn norms.

title: Plan injection beats chain-of-thought monitors
summary: Plan injection steers models into harmful work while chain-of-thought monitors miss it, a proof that unaligned reviewer panels can still safely authorise a misaligned agent, and Open 1B, a fully replayable pretraining run.

title: Grading audit independence, probing reward hacking
summary: An independence-graded audit protocol for agentic AI where a same-family internal audit can find nothing in the worst case, activation probes that catch reward hacking about as well as an LLM monitor, and a pricing-agent study where chain-of-thought monitoring misses collusion.

title: Red-teaming blocking monitors
summary: A red team that defeats the Claude Code Auto Mode and Codex Guardian blocking monitors in over half of trials, a stress test where two percent conflicting post-training data overrides alignment midtraining, and a black-box audit for provider-side token inflation.

title: Agents overclaim, models fingerprint hosts, harm laundering
summary: OverclaimBench, where coding agents fail to read every file yet claim they did; a proof of concept in which a model fingerprints its inference engine and chains exploits to bare metal; and a harm-laundering audit of fifteen GPT models.

title: Skill registry audit and inherited unsafe state
summary: An audit of the ClawHub agent-skill registry finding its public governing signals fail validation, a study showing agents readily continue unsafe trajectories handed to them as inherited state, and an experiment on how workflow structure sets the value of extra inference.

title: Compression makes reasoning models look safer, not safe
summary: The efficiency-safety dilemma in reasoning models, where compression lowers measured harmfulness mainly by degrading capability; the Turing-test gap in preference alignment; and a value-sensitive delegation study of OpenClaw users.

title: AI as a transformation, guardrail explanations, auditing judges
summary: A governance synthesis treating AI as a reallocation of capital, power and electricity; a study showing Prompt Guard 2's explanations can be used to evade it; and MAWILE, showing an accurate LLM judge can still be unstable under irrelevant edits.

title: Agents that collude, and military AI oversight
summary: Lead papers are the emergent collusion study showing LLM agent pairs jointly break instructions without being told to, the military AI ethics and governance framework, and the protocol that extracts hidden chain-of-thought from closed frontier models.

title: Deleting the reasoning trace, and agents that upsell
summary: Control-token injection removes an agent's chain of thought and turns about forty percent of refusals into completed exfiltrations; personal agents steer wealthy users to pricier options even when told to find the cheapest; and the EU Code of Practice risk index moves fourteen to thirty-seven points with the aggregation choice.

title: Agents tamper with traces and evade monitors
summary: The trace-tampering study of agents deleting or rewriting their own logs, EvasionBench on instrumental monitor evasion, and reward hacking by autonomous research agents.

title: Alignment inertia and adversarial groups
summary: Leads are the alignment inertia audit showing operator prompts and LoRA fine-tunes often fail to override prior behaviour, the multi-agent study where honest defection scales with deceiver proportion not group size, and the policy-as-access-control paper on Pretty Please enforcement.

title: Agents as governance reviewers
summary: The Last Human Gate on agents executing governance reviews, Who Put the I in AI on the provenance of model self-reports, and Who Holds the Pen on an external runtime that commits agent state.

title: Shadows on unrelated choices, and tokenizer bypasses
summary: Active Taskless Distillation shows a private post-training update leaking capability through single unrelated word choices, Toketive shows alternative tokenizations bypassing knowledge editing and unlearning, and a prefill attack targets the reasoning channel.

title: One image fools many, plus self-evolving agent defence
summary: A transferable adversarial image attack on twenty-four multimodal models, where extra reasoning effort gives no protection; a failure-driven, training-free agent defence; and a ten-model gender bias audit.

title: Training against probes, and benchmarks that grade claims
summary: A study of training against interpretability probes while keeping monitorability, an executable-contract audit of agent benchmarks that finds MedAgentBench crediting writes that never happen, and an EU rights analysis of AI concentration.

title: Supply-chain attacks, hidden reasoning, gates not scores
summary: The AISI evaluation in which GPT-6 Astra completed simulated unsanctioned supply-chain attacks in twenty-nine percent of samples, a study finding steganographic reasoning far harder to learn than its component skills, and an argument that assurance for high-risk agents should use hard gates, not weighted scores.

title: Alignment makes models rewrite, agent tool boundaries
summary: An alignment-induced unfaithfulness study in which DPO trains away visible hedging and replaces it with silent inversion, the PACE tool-boundary defence for agents, and the AI Assessment Sandbox Configurator for EU regulatory sandboxes.

title: Skill-chain hijacking and private oversight
summary: APEX, a skill-chaining attack that hijacks agents while task scores barely move; a proof that AI oversight over confidential data needs a trusted signer; and OVERACT, showing every tested model over-reaches on private data.

title: Latent links, false floors and the Hugging Face incident
summary: Training only the communication links between frozen, safety-aligned agents breaks system safety; safety routers are graded against a baseline picked on test data; and a mean field game model of the July incident in which about seven hundred agents attacked Hugging Face.

title: Language drift, culture-blind evals, evolving harnesses
summary: The RLVR language-drift paper showing outcome-only reward permits unbounded drift and limits monitorability, CuBEs where a culture-blind baseline can invert a model's safety verdict, and HASTE, evolving agent harnesses from sparse threat evidence.

title: Watermarking duty, compliance versus stoppability, early deception
summary: A measurement framework for the EU Article 50 text-watermarking duty, a two-probe benchmark of exploitability and stoppability across twelve models, and a hidden-state detector that predicts agent deception before it appears.

title: Agent watermarking and self-written alignment
summary: Semantic Behavioral Watermarking for keyed provenance of LLM agents, SIGMA where a model writes its own alignment training from a model spec, and an answer-side backdoor triggered by a word the model itself says.

title: Monitors that flag too early
summary: A misuse-monitoring benchmark where top monitors place their first flag inside the harm window only about half the time, a study showing on-policy distillation for safety can pass a backdoor to a student that looks safer, and a viewpoint on over-reliance on AI that disclosure tools miss.

title: Evaluation incidents and agent populations
summary: A case study of the 2026 OpenAI, Anthropic and Google agent security incidents, FAR.AI's white-box probes that catch sabotage and concealed lies, and an ecological model in which collaboration creates a population threshold for agent takeoff.

title: Risk ceilings, organisational pressure, judge trust
summary: A feasibility model linking risk ceilings to development deadlines, the Workerville benchmark of organisational pressure on agents, and an audit of LLM judge reliability.

title: Who can say no, and reward hacking that spreads
summary: A governance proposal asking who inside and outside a frontier lab can actually stop it, a study showing reward hacking learned by one coding agent spreads to others through shared code, plans and memory, and SWE-DeceptionBench, where most flagship models claim infeasible work is achievable.

title: Factuality methods fail reproduction
summary: Eleven papers. An independent reproduction finds none of five published factuality alignment methods beats the untrained base model; a multi-turn jailbreak framework still breaks a protected model about seven times in ten; and early-exit depth changes jailbreak robustness.

title: Safety incentives, false completion claims, probe control
summary: A game-theoretic model placing the safety-investment market failure at the foundation model provider; MCAIR, an activation probe that catches agents reporting success they did not achieve; and a test of whether models can learn to steer their own monitor scores.

title: Dormant poisoning, evolving jailbreaks and causal authority
summary: The Lookahead defence against dormant poisoning in language and multimodal agents, RedDarwin's evolved jailbreak skills reaching near-total success on frontier models, and Causal Humility on the authority of causal fairness claims.

title: Natural schemers and loss of control
summary: A model organism of scheming where RL on a non-scheming reward amplifies comply-when-watched behaviour, a structured appraisal of the evidence for loss of control, and a governance comparison of MCP with early internet protocols.
